22407553_6899c9aa.text: The anteroventral periventricular nucleus of the preoptic region of the hypothalamus (AVPV) contains a sexually dimorphic population of neurons that are known to be involved in regulation of reproductive functions such as preovulatory gonadotropin surge in female rodents and possible sex differences in puberty onset. One of the sexual dimorphic populations is tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) positive neurons which their number is grater in females compare to males.
